methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Climate & Energy (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 8 same-sector peers exist in Climate & Energy, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Ambrosia Energy is a Growth-stage private company in the Climate & Energy sector. The valuation universe comprises one public comparable (LNZA) and eight private peers, including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix. However, the peer set presents a structural constraint: no subset of same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier comparables yields three or more datapoints necessary for robust peer-median analysis.

The Peer-Median method is not applicable to this valuation. While eight same-sector private companies exist, none satisfy the narrowing filters required for credible triangulation. Filtering by stage, proximity, or valuation tier independently or in combination yields fewer than three matches, making a sector-wide median inappropriate given the heterogeneity in technology maturity, capital intensity, and commercialization timelines across Climate & Energy. Reliance on a diluted peer set would introduce material bias.

The current analysis cannot support a quantified valuation range. Additional data—including Ambrosia's funding history, revenue or customer traction metrics, and more granular positioning of the peer cohort across stage and valuation bands—would be necessary to enable alternative methods such as venture capital method, comparable transaction multiples, or refined peer-median analysis. At present, the sparsity of tight comparables and absence of disclosed financial or transactional benchmarks prevents defensible triangulation.
